record.paper_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
record.original_question: In Fe/MoS2 and other heterostructures that combine a non-van-der-Waals magnet with a defective or weakly magnetic van der Waals transition-metal dichalcogenide, how do charge transfer, magnetic proximity, orbital hybridization, defects, atomic diffusion, and dopant incorporation determine the interfacial magnetism, exchange-bias effect, and spin-transport response?

evidence.quote: It is also important to mention that the conductivity mismatch between the metal (Fe) and the semiconductor (MoS2) could promote charge transfer across the Fe/MoS2 interface and the Fe layer could magnetize the MoS2 monolayer via the MP effect--both of which were not included in these calculations.
However, the mechanism of charge transfer that mediates the magnetism and the origin of the EB effect in these systems are not fully understood.

Such a large discrepancy between experiment and theory suggests other possible contributions (surface roughness, magnetic proximity, atomic diffusion, doping) to the magnetism, charge transport, and spin transport in the FeNi/MoS2 system.

These studies yield further insights into spin manipulation in non-vdW magnet/vdW 2D-TMD heterostructures, but also raise open questions regarding the underlying origins of MP-mediated interfacial magnetism.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider a heterostructure consisting of a non-van-der-Waals ferromagnetic metal (such as Fe or FeNi) deposited on a monolayer or few-layer transition-metal dichalcogenide (TMD) such as MoS2, where the TMD may possess intrinsic point defects (e.g., sulfur vacancies), substitutional dopants, or otherwise weak/induced magnetism. Develop a quantitative theoretical framework that determines the interfacial magnetism, the exchange-bias effect (i.e., the horizontal shift of the magnetic hysteresis loop after field cooling), and the longitudinal and spin-polarized transport response of such an interface, by simultaneously accounting for: (i) interfacial charge transfer driven by the conductivity/work-function mismatch between the metallic ferromagnet and the semiconducting TMD; (ii) the magnetic proximity effect that induces spin polarization in the TMD layer; (iii) orbital hybridization between the 3d states of the ferromagnet and the d/p states of the TMD; (iv) the role of structural and chemical defects, including surface roughness and sulfur/chalcogen vacancies; (v) atomic interdiffusion across the interface; and (vi) chemical doping or substitutional incorporation of magnetic atoms into the TMD. Specifically, identify the dominant microscopic mechanism(s) responsible for the observed exchange-bias field and predict its magnitude, sign, and temperature dependence as a function of interfacial composition and defect density, and reconcile the quantitative discrepancy between first-principles predictions and experimentally measured exchange-bias and magnetoresistance values in Fe/MoS2 and FeNi/MoS2 systems.
artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns the microscopic origin of magnetic proximity, exchange bias, and spin transport at non-vdW ferromagnet/TMD interfaces (e.g., Fe/MoS2, FeNi/MoS2). The available literature explicitly describes these mechanisms as not fully understood, with ongoing experimental and theoretical work and persistent quantitative discrepancies between DFT predictions and measurements. No comprehensive, validated framework reconciling all listed contributions has been established, so the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in 2D vdW Magnetic Heterostructures
status_evidence.snippet: Open questions on charge transfer, magnetic proximity, and exchange bias at non-vdW magnet/TMD interfaces are highlighted as perspectives.
status_evidence.claim: The mechanisms underlying interfacial magnetism and exchange bias in Fe/MoS2-type systems are described as not fully understood.
